add.partOfSpeech: noun (feminine), absolute and construct, with and without suffixes
add.literal: adornment, beauty; that in which one glories or takes pride
add.standardEnglish: ASV 'the beauty of their anklets' (3:18), 'excellent and comely' (4:2, adjectival), 'the glory of his high looks' (10:12), 'the beauty of the Chaldeans' pride' (13:19), 'their glory' (20:5), 'according to the beauty of a man' (44:13); JPS 1917 'the bravery of their anklets' (3:18), 'the glory of his haughty looks' (10:12), 'the beauty of the Chaldeans' pride' (13:19), 'their glory' (20:5), 'according to the beauty of a man' (44:13); NJPS 'the finery' (3:18), 'majestic pride' (10:12), 'Proud splendor of the Chaldeans' (13:19), 'their boast' (20:5), 'The beauty of a man' (44:13) (Sefaria, checked 2026-11-26)
add.wohChoice: 'honor' is the book default for tip̄ʾereṯ (wave I-4 ruling 2; founder ruling 2026-11-26): 4:2 'pride and honor'; 20:5 'Egypt their honor'. The default keeps 'glory' for kāḇôḏ (kavod-nondivine-glory-isaiah), 'splendor' for hāḏār (hadar-splendor-isaiah), 'beauty' for ṣᵉḇî (tsevi-beauty-isaiah) and 'majesty' for gāʾôn. Recorded departures, where the idiom does not allow 'honor': 3:18 'the finery of the anklets' (ornament; daughters-of-zion-finery-isaiah-3); 10:12 'the boasting of his haughty looks' (pejorative, tied to the Hithpael 'boast itself' of 10:15; lexical-cruxes-isaiah-10); 13:19 'the splendor of the pride of the Chaldeans' (Babylon as the Chaldeans' ornament; NJPS 'Proud splendor'; 'beauty' is taken by ṣᵉḇî in the same verse); 44:13 'with the beauty of a human being' (the physical form of the idol; ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS 'beauty'). The stable departures are recorded, not reopened. Future sites take 'honor' unless their Editor records a departure here.
add.rationale: tip̄ʾereṯ is the ornament or beauty in which someone takes pride, and so also that pride itself, honour or boasting (BDB; HALOT; recalled). The English versions render it by context, 'beauty', 'glory', 'bravery', 'finery', 'boast' and 'splendor', and ASV's commonest choice, 'glory', would merge it with kāḇôḏ, which wave I-4 ruling 2 keeps strict. 'Honor' is the sense of the word in the triad 'for praise, for fame and for honor' (Deut 26:19; Jer 13:11), and the stable 4:2 and the wave I-4 20:5 already print it. At 20:5 the noun is what the people boasted in, Egypt as the power they relied on (NJPS 'their boast'), and 'their honor' gives that sense without 'glory'. Where 'honor' would invert or obscure the sense, the book has departed and the departures are listed in wohChoice so that a reader can audit them: an item of jewellery (3:18), the Assyrian king's arrogance (10:12), Babylon as ornament (13:19, where 'beauty' now renders ṣᵉḇî after the founder's ruling) and the beauty of the human form (44:13, which shares 'beauty' with ṣᵉḇî as a recorded collision). The entry was created at the wave I-4 sign-off (founder ruling 2026-11-26), as the chapter 20 Editor and Reviewer recommended, to take the tip̄ʾereṯ item out of the verse-scoped tsemach-yhwh-branch-isaiah-4. The renderings are standard glosses and carry no lens, so the claim is direct.

add.wohChoice: 'glory' for the noun kāḇôḏ also where it is the glory of persons, peoples and their possessions (wave I-4 ruling 2: 'glory' for kāḇôḏ is strict; founder ruling 2026-11-26): 4:2 'beauty and glory' (predicated of the growth of the land); 8:7 'the king of Assyria and all his glory'; 10:3 'where will you leave your glory?'; 10:16 'under his glory'; 10:18 'the glory of his forest'; 11:10 'his resting place shall be glory'; 14:18 'lie in glory'; 16:14 'the glory of Moab'; 17:3 'the glory of the children of Israel'; 17:4 'the glory of Jacob'; 21:16 'all the glory of Kedar'; 22:18 'the chariots of your glory'; 22:23 'a throne of glory'; 22:24 'all the glory of his father's house'. The senses of wealth, multitude, body and rank are given in commentary, not in the line, and the noun is kept where ASV turns it into an adjective (4:2; 11:10 'glorious'). One recorded departure: 5:13 kᵉḇôḏô 'their honored men' (stable; ASV, JPS 1917), where the noun is a collective for the nobility set against hămônô 'its multitude'. Outside this entry: the divine kāḇôḏ (central kavod-yhwh; overlay kevodo-kavod-suffixed-isaiah, kavod-labanah-chammah-isaiah-24); 4:5 'over all the glory', whose referent (Zion's glory or the divine presence) is disputed; and the verb and participles of kbd ('honor', 'the honored', 23:8-9).
add.rationale: kāḇôḏ comes from kbd 'be heavy', and of human beings it is their weight in the world: wealth (Gen 31:1), multitude, rank and splendour (BDB; HALOT; recalled). NJPS renders it by that contextual sense ('multitude', 'mass', 'body', 'substance', 'honor'), which interprets each site, while ASV and JPS 1917 print 'glory' at nearly every one of them. Wave I-4 ruling 2 makes 'glory' strict for kāḇôḏ so that one Hebrew noun keeps one English word across the book, and the stable chapters already apply it at 8:7, 10:3, 10:16, 10:18, 11:10 and 14:18. One English word also lets the reader see that the book uses the same noun for the glory of Assyria, Moab, Kedar, Jacob and Shebna (10:16-18; 16:14; 17:3-4; 21:16; 22:18) and for the glory of YHWH (6:3; 40:5). The one departure, 5:13 'their honored men', is ASV's and JPS 1917's rendering of a collective that names persons, where 'their glory are famished' is not English; it is recorded so that the concordance can be audited. The entry was created at the wave I-4 sign-off (founder ruling 2026-11-26) to gather the non-divine sites that earlier sat only in chapter-scoped entries (lexical-cruxes-isaiah-10, lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22). The rendering is the standard English of the PD versions and carries no lens, so the claim is direct.

(24:16) (Sefaria, checked 2026-11-26)
add.wohChoice: 'beauty' is the book default for ṣᵉḇî I, so that 'glory' stays reserved for kāḇôḏ (wave I-4 ruling 2; founder ruling 2026-11-26): 4:2 'beauty and glory'; 13:19 'Babylon, the beauty of kingdoms' (stable line revised 2026-11-26, chapter 13 version 1.0.1); 23:9 'to profane the pride of all beauty'. (stable; ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS 'Glory'), where the noun is the content of an acclamation and 'Beauty to the righteous one!' would not be English. The homonym ṣᵉḇî II 'gazelle' (13:14 'like a hunted gazelle') is outside the entry. Future sites (28:1, 4, 5 and later) take 'beauty' unless their Editor records a departure here.
add.rationale: ṣᵉḇî I is 'beauty, ornament, splendour' (BDB; HALOT; recalled), the land or city as a jewel (Ezek 20:6, 15; Dan 11:16 'the beautiful land'). ASV and JPS 1917 often render it 'glory', which in this book would merge it with kāḇôḏ, and the stable 4:2 already prints ṣᵉḇî 'beauty' beside kāḇôḏ 'glory' in the same verse. The chapter 23 Editor extended that choice to 23:9 ('the pride of all beauty'; NJPS 'all glorious beauty') and reported that the stable 13:19 and 24:16 printed 'glory'. The founder ruled on 2026-11-26 (wave I-4 sign-off, decision 8) to revise 13:19 to 'the beauty of kingdoms', a phrase where 'beauty' reads naturally and keeps Babylon's description in the ornament register of the verse, and to keep 24:16 'Glory to the righteous one!' as a recorded departure, because in an acclamation English uses 'Glory to …' and the line would otherwise become unidiomatic. The entry takes over the ṣᵉḇî item from the verse-scoped tsemach-yhwh-branch-isaiah-4, which keeps the ṣemaḥ decision. The renderings are standard glosses and carry no lens, so the claim is direct.

tsemach-yhwh-branch-isaiah-4.wohChoice: 'the branch of YHWH' in lower case, 'the fruit of the land'; the four lᵉ-predicates kept as nouns ('beauty and glory … pride and honor'), with tip̄ʾereṯ 'honor' so that 'splendor' stays reserved for hāḏār (overlay `hadar-splendor-isaiah`) and 'glory' for kāḇôḏ. The ṣᵉḇî, kāḇôḏ and tip̄ʾereṯ items are governed book-wide by tsevi-beauty-isaiah, kavod-nondivine-glory-isaiah and tiferet-honor-isaiah (founder ruling 2026-11-26). The royal ṣemaḥ of Jer 23:5; 33:15 and the name 'Branch' of Zech 3:8; 6:12 and the Targum's 'the Messiah of YHWH' are reported in commentary, not imposed by capitalisation.
tsemach-yhwh-branch-isaiah-4.rationale: ṣemaḥ is 'sprout, growth', what springs from the ground (BDB 855; HALOT 1034; Gen 19:25; Ezek 16:7; Ps 65:11), and in 4:2 it stands in synonymous parallel with pᵉrî hāʾāreṣ 'the fruit of the land', which favours the vegetation reading: the restored growth of the land as YHWH's gift to the survivors (Wildberger, Isaiah 1-12, 1991; Williamson, Isaiah 1-5, ICC 2006; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, AB 19, 2000). The messianic reading rests on the Targum ('the Messiah of YHWH'; defended by Oswalt, The Book of Isaiah 1-39, NICOT 1986) and on the later royal usage: in Jer 23:5; 33:15 the title is ṣemaḥ ṣaddîq lᵉḏāwiḏ 'a righteous branch for David', with David as the genitive, and in Zech 3:8; 6:12 'Branch' is a name ('my servant the Branch', 'a man whose name is Branch'); none of these has the construct ṣemaḥ YHWH, so the title cannot simply be read back into Isa 4:2. Capitalising 'Branch' would decide between the two readings in the English, which the Hebrew does not do; the lower case keeps ASV and NRSV and leaves the question to the commentary. ʾereṣ in pᵉrî hāʾāreṣ is the land of Israel (Num 13:20, 26; Deut 1:25), not the cosmic earth of overlay `eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24`, which stays scoped to ch. 24. The lᵉ-predicates (li-ṣḇî û-lᵉḵāḇôḏ … lᵉḡāʾôn û-lᵉṯip̄ʾereṯ) are rendered as nouns, the literal grammar, where ASV smooths them into adjectives; bare kāḇôḏ is the standard 'glory'. tip̄ʾereṯ ('beauty, glory, honour', BDB 802; HALOT) is rendered 'honor', its sense in the triad 'for praise, for fame and for honor' (Deut 26:19; Jer 13:11), because the wave I-1 overlay entry `hadar-splendor-isaiah` reserves 'splendor' for hāḏār (2:10, 19, 21; 53:2) and 'beauty' is ṣᵉḇî in the same verse; the change is a concordance fix. The signed-off 13:19 renders tip̄ʾereṯ 'splendor' ('the splendor of the pride of the Chaldeans'). By founder ruling 2026-11-26 (wave I-4 sign-off) that is recorded as a departure in the book-wide tiferet-honor-isaiah, and the ṣᵉḇî and kāḇôḏ items of this verse are carried book-wide by tsevi-beauty-isaiah and kavod-nondivine-glory-isaiah. This entry keeps the ṣemaḥ decision and the construction of 4:2.

choter-netser-geza-shoot-twig-stock-isai.wohChoice: 'a shoot out of the stock of Jesse, and a twig out of his roots shall bear fruit' (11:1): ḥōṭer 'shoot', gezaʿ 'stock' (as at 40:24), nēṣer 'twig' (JPS 1917, NJPS). 'branch' is reserved for ṣemaḥ (4:2, overlay tsemach-yhwh-branch-isaiah-4) and 'stump' for maṣṣeḇeṯ (6:13). Lower case; the royal and messianic reception (Targum; Matt 2:23 'Nazarene') is reported in commentary only. MT yip̄reh 'shall bear fruit' kept (mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah). Book rule for nēṣer (founder ruling 2026-11-26): never 'branch'; 'twig' at 11:1, where ḥōṭer already has 'shoot'; the stable 14:19 nēṣer nitʿāḇ reads 'a loathed shoot' (revised 2026-11-26, chapter 14 version 1.0.1), and 60:21 nēṣer maṭṭāʿay follows ('shoot'); ISA-60:21 is added to appliesTo when that line is made.
choter-netser-geza-shoot-twig-stock-isai.rationale: Isa 11:1 uses two growth words, ḥōṭer and nēṣer, and neither is the ṣemaḥ of 4:2. ḥōṭer occurs elsewhere only at Prov 14:3, where it is a rod or switch; nēṣer is a sprout or offshoot (BDB; HALOT; Isa 14:19; 60:21; Dan 11:7). ASV renders nēṣer 'branch', but JPS 1917 and NJPS render it 'twig', so the line follows a standard Jewish translation and keeps 'branch' for ṣemaḥ, the word that becomes the royal title in Jer 23:5; 33:15 and Zech 3:8; 6:12. Keeping the two lemmas apart in English lets a reader see that Isa 11:1 does not use the title-word, which is a fact about the Hebrew, not a reading of it. gezaʿ 'stock' follows ASV and JPS 1917 and matches the stable 40:24 'their stock'; NJPS 'stump' is recorded, and 'stump' stays with maṣṣeḇeṯ at 6:13. The stable 14:19 rendered nēṣer nitʿāḇ 'a loathed branch' (ASV 'an abominable branch'; JPS 1917 'an abhorred offshoot'). By founder ruling 2026-11-26 (wave I-3), applied with the wave I-4 sign-off, 14:19 now reads 'a loathed shoot' (chapter 14 version 1.0.1) and is in appliesTo; 60:21 nēṣer maṭṭāʿay follows when chapter 60 is drafted, so that 'branch' stays with ṣemaḥ throughout the book. The verb yip̄reh is MT (prh 'bear fruit'); LXX anabēsetai and Vulgate ascendet presuppose 'come up / sprout' and are reported in commentary.

rider-of-the-clouds-rkb-arpt-cross-corpu.partOfSpeech: Ugaritic divine epithet: rkb ʿrpt 'Rider of the Clouds', the standing storm-theophany epithet of Baʿlu throughout the Cycle (project edition baal-cycle-woh, KTU 1.1-1.4, line numbers as printed there: KTU 1.2-iv:6, 1.3-ii:40, 1.3-iv:23, 1.4-vi:10); MAJOR cross-corpus to Hebrew Bible storm-theophany vocabulary applied to YHWH (Ps 68:5 rōkēb bā-ʿărābôt; Deut 33:26; Ps 18:11; Isa 19:1)
rider-of-the-clouds-rkb-arpt-cross-corpu.rationale:
**THE central epithet of Baʿlu.** Ugaritic *rkb ʿrpt* 'Rider of the Clouds' is the most-attested standing storm-theophany epithet of Baʿlu across the entire Ugaritic corpus. In the Baal Cycle KTU 1.1-1.2 it appears at KTU 1.2-iv:6 (Kothar's address: *ṯnt l rkb ʿrpt* 'did I not repeat to you, O Rider of the Clouds?'). The epithet recurs at KTU 1.3-ii:40, 1.3-iv:23 and 1.4-vi:10. These are the only sites where the project's edition (baal-cycle-woh, KTU 1.1-1.4; line numbers as printed there) prints rkb ʿrpt, checked 2026-11-26. Further occurrences in the tablets the project has not edited (KTU 1.5-1.6) are not verified here. BCY-WOH-1.4-vii:32 (ytn qlh b ʿrpt 'He gives forth his voice in the clouds') is not an epithet site. It stays in appliesTo because that line cites this entry as storm-theophany context. The image is the storm-god riding on cloud-mounts as his theophany-vehicle: the cloud-as-divine-chariot motif. *rkb* 'rider' is the standard Northwest-Semitic noun for 'one who rides / mounts'; *ʿrpt* is the plural of *ʿrp* 'cloud', possibly a poetic-or-archaic plural form.

**The most-clearly-Ugaritic-derived Hebrew Bible storm-theophany.** The cross-corpus link to the Hebrew Bible is among the most-documented and the textually clearest in Northwest-Semitic-Hebrew comparative-philology:
- **Ps 68:5** — *šîrû lē-ʾlōhîm zammĕrû šĕmô sōllû lā-rōkēb bā-ʿărābôt b-Yāh šĕmô* 'sing to Elohim, praise his name; lift up a song to the one who rides on the clouds — Yah is his name'. The phrase *rōkēb bā-ʿărābôt* has been read in two ways: (i) **'rider on the clouds'** reading *ʿărābôt* as a Hebrew counterpart to Ugaritic *ʿrpt* 'clouds' (the standard modern critical reading, Cross 1973; Day 2000; Tate 1990); (ii) **'rider on the deserts'** reading *ʿărābôt* as the plural of *ʿărābâ* 'desert' (the older traditional reading, ASV; KJV 'rider in the deserts'). The modern critical reading takes the Hebrew *ʿărābôt* as etymologically and functionally the same as Ugaritic *ʿrpt* — clouds, with the Hebrew vocalization reflecting the Hebrew development of the lexeme. This is the **single clearest textual borrowing** of Baʿlu's epithet for YHWH in the Hebrew Bible.
- **Deut 33:26** — *rōkēb šāmayim b-ʿezrekha u-v-gaʾavato šĕchaqim* 'he rides the heavens for your help, in his majesty the clouds' — Moses' blessing of Israel; the *rōkēb šāmayim* 'rider of the heavens' is a near-synonymous variant.
- **Ps 18:11 (// 2 Sam 22:11)** — *va-yirkav ʿal kĕruv va-yaʿof va-yedeʾ ʿal kanfei ruach* 'he rode on a cherub and flew, swooping on the wings of the wind' — the storm-theophany in the cherub-and-wind variant; structurally parallel to the cloud-mount but using cherub-throne imagery.
- **Ps 104:3** — *ha-śam ʿabim rĕkhubô ha-mhalekh ʿal kanfei ruach* 'who makes the clouds his chariot, who walks on the wings of the wind' — directly cognate imagery, with *ʿabim* 'clouds' + *rĕkhubô* 'his chariot'.
- **Isa 19:1** — *hinneh YHWH rōkēb ʿal ʿab qal* 'behold YHWH rides on a swift cloud' (in the oracle against Egypt).
- **Dan 7:13** — *ʿim ʿănanê šĕmayyāʾ k-bar ʾĕnāš ātēh hăwāʾ* 'one like a son of man came with the clouds of heaven' (in the throne-room vision).
- **Mark 14:62 // Matt 26:64; Rev 1:7** — the NT 'coming on the clouds' Christological appropriation of Dan 7:13.

The named-scholarship treats the Ugaritic *rkb ʿrpt* → Hebrew *rōkēb bā-ʿărābôt* / *rōkēb šāmayim* / Baʿlu-storm-imagery-for-YHWH as **one of the textually clearest cases of Baʿlu-epithet-absorption-into-Yahwistic-theology**. The historical-religious process is the same one documented at the central entry on Baʿlu: as Yahweh's storm-god profile sharpens (especially in the monarchic period), Baʿlu's epithets are progressively reassigned to YHWH.

**Named-scholarship frame.** **F. M. Cross**, *Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic* (Cambridge MA 1973), pp. 147-194 on the storm-theophany inheritance. **J. Day**, *Yahweh and the Gods and Goddesses of Canaan* (JSOTSup 265, Sheffield 2000), pp. 91-127 on Baʿal and YHWH-as-storm-god. **M. E. Tate**, *Psalms 51-100* (WBC, Waco 1990) on Ps 68. **D. M. Howard**, *The Structure of Psalms 93-100* (BJSUCSD 5, Winona Lake 1997) on the cloud-theophany psalms. **M. S. Smith**, *The Ugaritic Baal Cycle, Volume 1* (1994) on the Ugaritic epithet itself. **N. Wyatt**, 'Cloud,' in DDD (2nd ed., Leiden 1999).

**Bidirectional cross-references.** Cluster with new Ugaritic entries `baal-ugaritic-baalu-storm-god-cross-corpus-hebrew-bible-polemic`, `mount-sapunu-tsafon-cosmic-mountain-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible`; existing Hebrew central entries dealing with storm-theophany (no dedicated central entry yet; future Hebrew Editor pass on Ps 68:5 should produce one with bidirectional back-reference).

**Lens-discipline operational disavowals.** (i) **No Christological pre-resolution.** The NT 'coming on the clouds' Christological appropriation of Dan 7:13 (Mark 14:62; Matt 26:64; Rev 1:7) is a second-order theological-historical development resting on Dan 7:13 which itself rests on the Hebrew Bible storm-theophany tradition which itself absorbs Ugaritic *rkb ʿrpt*. The Editor does **not** pre-resolve the Ugaritic and Hebrew material to the NT Christological reception; the typological reading is a downstream layer that lives in wiki and broader-corpus discussions. (ii) **No Sitchin-corpus reading of cloud-riding as Anunnaki-aerial-vehicle / cloud-ship / atmospheric-craft.** The Ugaritic source-text deploys *rkb ʿrpt* in the standard Northwest-Semitic storm-theophany register; the cloud-mount is the Bronze Age West-Semitic theological-mythological image of the storm-god riding the storm-clouds, not an engineering-vehicle vocabulary.
